report: Resident A was assisted with brushing teeth and preparing for the day. Discovered a 3cm area of peeling skin with mild redness on the right heel. Resident expressed discomfort while moving. Pain control measures reviewed, and resident encouraged to rest. Care plan updated to include more frequent skin assessments.

Resident B required full assistance with eating breakfast. Noted difficulty swallowing, resulting in two episodes of choking. Speech and language therapist to be consulted for evaluation of swallowing function. Resident appeared lethargic, requiring gentle encouragement to eat.

Resident C was observed to be restless and wandering in the hallway at night. Upon being guided back to bed, resident expressed feeling of tightness in the chest. Vital signs monitored and GP notified. Awaiting evaluation to adjust palliative care pain management plan.

Resident D had a complaint of intense nausea during the morning. Provided with anti-nausea medication as prescribed, and symptoms monitored throughout the day. Resident’s fluid intake documented, and additional hydration encouraged. Consultation with hospice nurse planned for a review of symptom control.

Resident E presented with increased agitation and confusion this morning, refusing assistance with personal hygiene. Visible pressure ulcer on the right buttock discovered, now measuring 4cm. Wound dressings applied following wound care protocol. Notified tissue viability nurse for assessment and management plan.

Louise was assisted with a wash this morning. It was discovered that she had a 5cm lesion to her left buttock that contains slough and appears infected. A swab was taken and a wound chart commenced. Inadine and Leukomed (wound dressings) in situ at present. Awaiting review from Tissue Viability Nurse.

Mr. Anderson appeared restless and agitated during the night. He wandered out of his room multiple times, requiring assistance to return. His confusion was more prominent today, and he needed continual reassurance. Family has been informed, and a care plan discussion is scheduled for tomorrow.

Mrs. Klein did not eat much of her meals today. She requires encouragement and full assistance with feeding. Observed coughing while drinking, necessitating the use of a modified swallow technique. Kept close hydration and nutrition monitoring lists updated.

Charles had visitors today, bringing a slight improvement in his mood. However, his pain levels have been fluctuating, with increased complaints of back pain in the evening. Pain relief medication was administered as per his care plan, but further assessment is required to ensure optimal pain management.

Dorothy's skin continues to show signs of oedema and redness. Most notably, a pressure ulcer has developed on her left heel. The wound care team has been notified, and current dressings were replaced. Added notes to her care plan indicating daily skin checks and additional pressure relief measures.

Resident A was assisted with a shower this morning. Noticed an area of peeling and redness on the left heel, likely a pressure sore. The wound was cleaned and dressed with Mepore. Resident also complained of mild nausea after breakfast, encouraged small sips of water and ginger tea. Family requested an update on medication changes, to be discussed with the physician.

Resident B was restless last night, frequently wandering in the corridor. Provided encouragement to return to bed multiple times. Noted increased confusion during the night; appeared more oriented this morning. Assisted with personal hygiene and dental care this morning. Due to difficulty in swallowing, used adaptive cutlery during breakfast and encouraged small bites.

Resident C showed signs of increased agitation in the afternoon, repeatedly fidgeting with clothing. Redirected to a quiet, low-stimulation environment which seemed to help. Had minimal interest in participating in group activities. Complained of back pain despite regular analgesic schedule, plan to review pain management with the medical team. Encouraged fluid intake to avoid dehydration.

Resident D received visitors from family for a brief period. Assistance provided with brushing teeth and washing in the morning. Exhibited mild confusion during daytime activity sessions. Appeared tired and lethargic after lunch, allowed extra rest time. Swelling noted in feet and lower legs, likely oedema; elevated legs on a pillow, awaiting further evaluation.

Resident E required full assistance with breakfast, including use of adaptive cutlery. Choked mildly on a piece of toast but recovered quickly. Observed mood swings from apathy to mild agitation throughout the day. Provided comfort and repositioning in the wheelchair to alleviate pressure points. Noted long fingernails which were trimmed to prevent scratching. Met with the Tissue Viability Nurse to review previous wound care treatments.

Mrs. Johnson required full assistance with washing and dressing this morning. Observed a 4cm pressure ulcer on her right ankle, presenting with redness and mild oozing. A clean dressing with Alginate was applied. Awaiting further evaluation by the Tissue Viability Nurse. Despite apathy, she managed to eat half of her breakfast when encouraged.

During his morning routine, Mr. Stevens displayed restlessness and confusion. He was aided with showering and using the toilet. A slight increase in oedema was noted in his lower legs. He experienced shortness of breath when walking to the dining room and was provided with his inhaler, which offered some relief. His care assistant provided adaptive cutlery for him at lunch, but his appetite was poor.

Mrs. Turner was agitated and needed reassurance throughout the night. She became disoriented, calling for her family, and needed support to settle back into bed. She accepted a small portion of porridge for breakfast with encouragement. Staff noticed her nails are overgrown; a request for the podiatrist was made. She reports moderate back pain, which has been managed with paracetamol.

Mr. Raymond appeared somnolent and had trouble keeping hydrated despite verbal prompts. Helped with cleaning his dental prostheses and dressing for the day. He received visitors in the afternoon which improved his mood slightly. He has been experiencing increased abdominal discomfort and diarrhea; arrangements are made for review by the attending GP.

Ms. Greene fell while attempting to transfer from her bed to the wheelchair. She was assisted back to bed safely, and no visible injuries were found except mild redness on her left knee. She refused breakfast and only drank minimal water upon insistence. She was later calmed by browsing through a magazine. Her pain level remains consistent, and she reports no new symptoms. Staff will continue to monitor for changes.

This afternoon, Marvin was assisted with brushing his teeth and getting ready for the night. Despite full assistance, he showed signs of restlessness and complained of back pain. We provided Marvin with a walking aid to alleviate his discomfort, but he remains slightly agitated. Discussion about his ongoing palliative care needs is scheduled.

Sarah had a poor appetite today and required full help during meals. Despite encouragement and the use of adapted cutlery, she barely consumed half of her food. Additionally, she exhibited mild confusion and seemed disoriented when trying to engage in a magazine. Care plan adjustments are being evaluated to address her nutritional and cognitive needs.

Elaine experienced severe shortness of breath throughout the evening, necessitating lying down on her side to breathe easier. She received a moderate level of help with personal care, including washing and dressing, but seemed unusually apathetic. Our team is closely monitoring her palliative care status and is coordinating with her family for further support.

Leonard needed help with cleaning his dental prostheses today. During interaction, he appeared significantly confused and required persistent guidance. He also complained of persistent nausea, which impacted his ability to participate in any organized activities. His medication orders are being reviewed to better manage these symptoms within his palliative care plan.

This morning, Agnes was assisted with a thorough wash and dressing. A pressure ulcer was observed on her right heel and a swab was taken to check for possible infection. Agnes showed signs of increased pain and distress when mobilizing with her wheelchair. She will need a thorough review from the Tissue Viability Nurse and a possible update in her care plan to manage her palliative care requirements.
